additional_issue_found: Standalone Windows IPC Clippy initially failed because windows-sys lacked Win32_System_IO, required for ReadFile and ConnectNamedPipe. The crate feature list was corrected; the subsequent check passed.

transport_review.server_authentication: Before sending the media capability, the client verifies kernel server PID against the parent PID, validates parent creation time against worker creation time, compares current-user SIDs and checks protected owner-only pipe owner/DACL. SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION prevents server impersonation using the client token.
transport_review.security_object_type: GetSecurityInfo receives SE_KERNEL_OBJECT and a live pipe HANDLE. Microsoft documents that GetSecurityInfo/SetSecurityInfo support all kernel-object types; its securable-object table explicitly lists named pipes.
transport_review.stop_concurrency: PIPE_NOWAIT writes have no outstanding overlapped I/O. The writer reads atomic running between immediate writes and sleeps at most 5 ms under backpressure. Worker destruction sets running=false and joins the writer before MediaPipe destroys its HANDLE; there is no concurrent handle close/write.
transport_review.send_deadline: Each pipe write call uses one steady-clock 250 ms packet deadline across partial writes. Polling and OS scheduling can add small deadline observation latency; Windows wall-clock behavior was not measured.
transport_review.unix_tcp_compatibility: Existing Unix transport and standalone loopback TCP fixture remain; Hub is not changed to TCP.

limitations: No Windows or Linux program was executed by these checks.
The Windows C++ check is syntax/type checking of platform.h using MinGW Win32 declarations and read-only host libc++ headers, not a complete worker cross-build or link check.
The actual Windows NamedPipe connection, parent/SID/DACL rejection, timeout/stop behavior, and full worker startup remain unverified on Windows.
Clippy validates target-specific Rust branches but does not run target tests.
